questions.q: What does uniqueness measure as a data quality dimension?
options: Whether each real-world entity is represented by exactly one record
Whether a record's values are correctly formatted
Whether a record's values match the real-world fact
Whether all required fields in a record have a value
questions.explain: Uniqueness is about record count per entity — not zero (completeness) and not more than one (duplicates) — independent of whether each individual copy is accurate or valid.

questions.q: In `GROUP BY Email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1`, what does the `HAVING` clause do that a `WHERE` clause couldn't in this query?
options: It filters on an aggregated value (COUNT) computed after grouping, which WHERE cannot do
It removes NULL values from the Email column before grouping
It sorts the results by Email alphabetically
It converts the Email column to uppercase for comparison
questions.explain: HAVING filters groups based on an aggregate result like COUNT(*); WHERE filters individual rows before aggregation and cannot reference an aggregate like COUNT(*) directly.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an exact duplicate and a fuzzy duplicate?
options: An exact duplicate matches character-for-character; a fuzzy duplicate represents the same entity without matching exactly
An exact duplicate can only occur in numeric columns; a fuzzy duplicate only in text columns
A fuzzy duplicate is always a data entry error; an exact duplicate never is
There is no difference — both terms describe the same kind of row
questions.explain: Exact duplicates are identical on the compared columns and are solvable with plain GROUP BY; fuzzy duplicates like 'Jon Smith' vs. 'John Smith' need similarity scoring or standardization first.

questions.q: In the ROW_NUMBER() de-duplication query, what does the condition `WHERE rn > 1` select?
options: Every row in a duplicate group except the first occurrence (by the ORDER BY)
Only the first occurrence of each duplicate group
Rows where the Email column is NULL
Rows where CustomerId is greater than 1
questions.explain: ROW_NUMBER() partitioned by Email and ordered by CustomerId assigns 1 to the first row per group and increasing numbers after; rn > 1 isolates the 'extra' duplicate rows beyond the first.

questions.q: Why does this lesson defer fuzzy duplicate matching to a later chapter instead of covering it alongside exact duplicates?
options: Fuzzy matching requires cleansing and standardization first, which is covered in Lesson 24
Fuzzy duplicates cannot occur in SQL Server databases
Fuzzy matching is not a real data quality concern
GROUP BY already fully solves fuzzy duplicate detection
questions.explain: The lesson explains that fuzzy duplicates need similarity scoring or standardized comparison keys, which depends on data cleansing techniques taught in Lesson 24, not plain T-SQL grouping.
